blockers.description: WR-05: destination "." passes both the manifest.schema.json pattern AND refuse_unsafe_destination, then crashes apply_disposition with an unhandled IsADirectoryError (not in cli.py's except tuple). Contradicts 27.1's own 'clean refusal, never a traceback' goal.
blockers.workaround: Fails closed — no unauthorized write. Reproduce: apply_disposition({'destination':'.','disposition':'create'}, tmpdir, payload=b'x')

blockers.description: WR-06: approval.check_valid still raises uncaught (JSONDecodeError/KeyError) on a corrupted or incomplete approval.json. WR-02's fix only wrapped _recompute_draft_hash; the json.loads at approval.py:181 and the stored[...] key accesses are outside the try.
blockers.workaround: Fails closed. Fix: widen the try to cover the read + key accesses.

blockers.description: WR-07: the WR-01 concurrency test would still pass if fcntl.flock() were deleted — it only asserts the .lock sidecar file exists, which open() alone creates. A test that cannot fail when the control regresses.
blockers.workaround: None. This is the same defect class that produced both Phase 27 and 27.1 — highest-priority of the three despite lowest severity label.

decisions.decision: secret_patterns[1] digit requirement relaxed to 2-of-3 charset classes
decisions.rationale: The evidence-redaction plaintext-leak harm outranks the false-positive cost; ci.yml red-green proof re-run to confirm 26.1's original false positive stays closed

decisions.decision: IGNORECASE collapse fixed with scoped (?-i:...) groups, consumers keep re.IGNORECASE
decisions.rationale: Repo targets Python >=3.11; fixes the pattern rather than every call site

decisions.decision: Adoption batch is purely additive evidence — no transitions.json edit
decisions.rationale: ADOPT-04..07 never mention phase-gating; transitions.json is constitution-plane, so adding a gate is a separate larger decision
Same-day re-discover against an unchanged ref resumes the same batch, satisfying SC-1's safe-resume

decisions.decision: approval.schema.json is a NEW self-contained contract, not an extension of attestation.schema.json
decisions.rationale: Attestation binds constraint-source files at SPEC time; approval binds a human promotion decision at REVIEW time — different vocabularies, no cross-file $ref

decisions.decision: New choke point refuse_unsafe_destination; refuse_if_constitution kept as a thin wrapper
decisions.rationale: Every write funnels through one guard; Phase 27's tests keep passing unmodified because they were insufficient, not wrong

decisions.decision: check_valid(repo_root=...) is the harness's own repo root, not the brownfield target
decisions.rationale: The approval's git_ref sits on the same plane as task_revision and draft_hash (all harness-side); a brownfield target may not be a git repo at all

decisions.decision: Case-insensitive constitution compare is always-on, never sys.platform-conditional
decisions.rationale: CI is Linux (case-sensitive), dev is macOS (case-insensitive); the guard must refuse identically on both

context_notes: Phase 27 is deliberately left as Executed-not-Complete with a failed verification on record — that is accurate history, not an oversight; do not retro-mark it complete. Its three security defects were closed by Phase 27.1, which passed 5/5. The through-line of this whole session: three separate phases (26.1->26.2, 27->27.1) shipped green while the changed control was wrong, every time because the tests only exercised the one input spelling that worked. WR-07 is that same defect still live. Treat 'would this test fail if the fix were reverted?' as the default question for any control-shaped change in this repo. Both constitution-plane commits this session (approval.schema.json, manifest.schema.json pattern) were human-ratified in-session, recorded distinctly from the HARNESS_DEV_BYPASS mechanical write.
